questions.stem: This infographic surrounds a cigarette with everyday products (lighter fluid, nail polish remover, battery metal, poison, toilet cleaner, car exhaust). What key point about tobacco smoke does it convey?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tobacco smoke provides essential nutrients

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cigarette smoke contains only nicotine and tar

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cigarette smoke contains numerous toxic chemicals

choices.label: D
choices.text: A single chemical accounts for all smoking harm

choices.label: E
choices.text: The listed chemicals are harmless flavor additives

explanation.summary: The figure pairs smoke constituents (e.g., butane, acetone, cadmium, arsenic, ammonia, carbon monoxide) with familiar toxic products to show that cigarette smoke is a mixture of many harmful chemicals.
explanation.whyCorrect: The figure pairs smoke constituents (e.g., butane, acetone, cadmium, arsenic, ammonia, carbon monoxide) with familiar toxic products to show that cigarette smoke is a mixture of many harmful chemicals.

questions.stem: This body diagram links tobacco smoking to disease in the mouth, larynx, esophagus, lungs, heart, stomach, pancreas, bladder, and arteries. What overall pattern of harm does it demonstrate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Smoking harms only the cardiovascular system

choices.label: B
choices.text: Smoking causes a single localized cancer

choices.label: C
choices.text: Smoking causes multi-organ, systemic disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Smoking has no proven organ effects

choices.label: E
choices.text: Smoking harms only the lungs

explanation.summary: Because carcinogens and toxins from smoke are absorbed and circulated, tobacco use raises risk of cancers and chronic disease across many organ systems, not just the lungs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because carcinogens and toxins from smoke are absorbed and circulated, tobacco use raises risk of cancers and chronic disease across many organ systems, not just the lungs.

questions.stem: This small, flat, USB-drive-shaped black device with a mouthpiece and pod is shown. What is it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A USB flash drive

choices.label: B
choices.text: A glucose meter

choices.label: C
choices.text: An electronic cigarette

choices.label: D
choices.text: A metered-dose asthma inhaler

choices.label: E
choices.text: An insulin injector pen

explanation.summary: The pod-style form factor with a mouthpiece identifies an electronic cigarette, which aerosolizes a nicotine-containing liquid for inhalation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pod-style form factor with a mouthpiece identifies an electronic cigarette, which aerosolizes a nicotine-containing liquid for inhalation.

questions.stem: This midsagittal brain diagram traces nicotine entering the brain, stimulating receptors in the ventral tegmental area, then dopamine release toward the nucleus accumbens and prefrontal cortex. Which mechanism of nicotine dependence does this illustrate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A noradrenergic surge from the locus coeruleus

choices.label: B
choices.text: GABAergic inhibition of the motor cortex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Activation of the mesolimbic dopamine reward pathway

choices.label: D
choices.text: Blockade of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Depletion of serotonin in the raphe nuclei

explanation.summary: Nicotine binds nicotinic receptors on VTA neurons, increasing dopamine release into the nucleus accumbens; this mesolimbic reward circuit reinforces use and drives addiction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nicotine binds nicotinic receptors on VTA neurons, increasing dopamine release into the nucleus accumbens; this mesolimbic reward circuit reinforces use and drives addiction.
